articles.title: India records 38% drop in TB mortality since 2015: WHO report
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: World Health Organization’s Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 showed a total of 1.13 million people died from tuberculosis last year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India has seen a 38% reduction in tuberculosis (TB) mortality since 2015, compared to a global average of 35%, and a 94% treatment success rate among patients with drug-susceptible TB, according to the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report 2026. Last year, the South-East Asia Region recorded the largest number of new TB cases (35%), followed by the Western Pacific Region (27%) and the African Region (25%). Around 88% of new TB cases occurred in 30 countries. India (about a quarter), Indonesia (10%), the Philippines (6.8%), China (6.5%), Pakistan (6.4%), Nigeria (4.9%), the Democratic Republic of the Congo (3.9%) and Bangladesh (3.7%) accounted for about a q of the global total. Globally, about 50% of people treated for TB and their households face total costs (direct medical expenditures, non-medical expenditures, and indirect costs such as income losses) that are catastrophic (greater than 20% of total household income). People with compromised immune systems, such as those living with HIV, undernutrition or diabetes, or people who use tobacco have a higher risk of falling ill. An estimated 9.6 lakh new TB cases were attributable to undernutrition, 9.2 lakh to diabetes, 7.3 lakh to alcohol use disorders, 6.9 lakh to smoking and 5.5 lakh to HIV infection. The report showed a total of 1.13 million people died from TB in 2025. Globally, TB is the world’s leading cause of death from a single infectious agent. Last year, an estimated 10.6 million people fell ill with TB worldwide, including 5.7 million men, 3.7 million women and 1.2 million children. Multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) remains a public health crisis and a health security threat. Only about two in five people with drug-resistant TB received treatment in 2025. Global efforts to combat TB have saved an estimated 86 million lives since 2000. Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by bacteria that most often affects the lungs. It spreads through the air when people with TB cough, sneeze or spit. TB is preventable and curable. Between December 7, 2024 and November 8, 2026, the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan achieved significant progress, identifying and bringing over 25 crore individuals within the scope of screening activities.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “India’s reduction in TB mortality has been the result of interventions under the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP), including proactive case finding including use of AI-enabled X-rays, rapid diagnostics, prompt treatment initiation, differentiated TB care, and nutritional support through the Nikshay Poshan Yojana and Nikshay Mitra initiative. These interventions were supported by AI tools for identification of hotspots, prediction of high-risk TB cases prone for adverse outcomes, Khushi – AI Chatbot & Avatar Videobot, etc.,” the Union Health Ministry statement said.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (12 NOV)

📰 India records 38% drop in TB mortality since 2015: WHO report

📌 Published: 12 Nov 2026, 11:20:12 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: World Health Organization’s Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 showed a total of 1.13 million people died from tuberculosis last year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India has seen a 38% reduction in tuberculosis (TB) mortality since 2015, compared to a global average of 35%, and a 94% treatment success rate among patients with drug-susceptible TB, according to the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report 2026. Last year, the South-East Asia Region recorded the largest number of new TB cases (35%), followed by the Western Pacific Region (27%) and the African Region (25%). Around 88% of new TB cases occurred in 30 countries. India (about a quarter), Indonesia (10%), the Philippines (6.8%), China (6.5%), Pakistan (6.4%), Nigeria (4.9%), the Democratic Republic of the Congo (3.9%) and Bangladesh (3.7%) accounted for about a q of the global total. Globally, about 50% of people treated for TB and their households face total costs (direct medical expenditures, non-medical expenditures, and indirect costs such as income losses) that are catastrophic (greater than 20% of total household income). People with compromised immune systems, such as those living with HIV, undernutrition or diabetes, or people who use tobacco have a higher risk of falling ill. An estimated 9.6 lakh new TB cases were attributable to undernutrition, 9.2 lakh to diabetes, 7.3 lakh to alcohol use disorders, 6.9 lakh to smoking and 5.5 lakh to HIV infection. The report showed a total of 1.13 million people died from TB in 2025. Globally, TB is the world’s leading cause of death from a single infectious agent. Last year, an estimated 10.6 million people fell ill with TB worldwide, including 5.7 million men, 3.7 million women and 1.2 million children. Multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) remains a public health crisis and a health security threat. Only about two in five people with drug-resistant TB received treatment in 2025. Global efforts to combat TB have saved an estimated 86 million lives since 2000. Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by bacteria that most often affects the lungs. It spreads through the air when people with TB cough, sneeze or spit. TB is preventable and curable. Between December 7, 2024 and November 8, 2026, the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan achieved significant progress, identifying and bringing over 25 crore individuals within the scope of screening activities.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “India’s reduction in TB mortality has been the result of interventions under the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP), including proactive case finding including use of AI-enabled X-rays, rapid diagnostics, prompt treatment initiation, differentiated TB care, and nutritional support through the Nikshay Poshan Yojana and Nikshay Mitra initiative. These interventions were supported by AI tools for identification of hotspots, prediction of high-risk TB cases prone for adverse outcomes, Khushi – AI Chatbot & Avatar Videobot, etc.,” the Union Health Ministry statement said.

Predictably (Adverb)
जैसा पहले से अनुमान था — बिना किसी आश्चर्य के बिल्कुल पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक होना।
✓ Syn: Foreseeably, Expectedly, Inevitably  |  ✖ Ant: Unexpectedly, Surprisingly, Abruptly
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
Undernutrition (Adjective / Verb)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Undernutrition' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Identification (Noun)
पहचान — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Identification' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

articles.title: ISRO successfully carries out ground static test of PSLV third stage
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The configuration of the third stage was revisited comprehensively with respect to the design margins, raw material acceptance criteria, assembly procedures, and the quality checks that were followed so far

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) which is looking to get its workhorse launcher, the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV), back on track has successfully carried out the ground static test of the PSLV third stage (PS3) at the Static Test Facility in Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota on Thursday (November 12, 2026). “Subsequent to the anomalies observed in the third stage of PSLV during the PSLV-C61/EOS-09 & PSLV-C62 / EOS-N1 missions, the configuration of the PS3 stage was revisited comprehensively with respect to the design margins, raw material acceptance criteria, assembly procedures, and the quality checks that were followed so far,” ISRO said. “The configuration has been strengthened and essential improvements have been carried out in the nozzle configuration to improve design margins along with updated procedures in the acceptance of raw materials, assembly procedures and quality checks,” ISRO added. It also said that the mechanical interfaces have been strengthened with redundancy in the sealing systems and adequacy of the design margins have been verified. “The updates in assembly procedures and non-destructive tests (NDT) during the various phases of integration and transportation have been implemented and the new version of the PS3 solid motor stage is realised and tested successfully,” ISRO said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Based on the detailed analysis and reviews of the test data, the space agency said further tests are planned.

📰 ISRO successfully carries out ground static test of PSLV third stage

1. Core Context & Background: The configuration of the third stage was revisited comprehensively with respect to the design margins, raw material acceptance criteria, assembly procedures, and the quality checks that were followed so far

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) which is looking to get its workhorse launcher, the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV), back on track has successfully carried out the ground static test of the PSLV third stage (PS3) at the Static Test Facility in Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota on Thursday (November 12, 2026). “Subsequent to the anomalies observed in the third stage of PSLV during the PSLV-C61/EOS-09 & PSLV-C62 / EOS-N1 missions, the configuration of the PS3 stage was revisited comprehensively with respect to the design margins, raw material acceptance criteria, assembly procedures, and the quality checks that were followed so far,” ISRO said. “The configuration has been strengthened and essential improvements have been carried out in the nozzle configuration to improve design margins along with updated procedures in the acceptance of raw materials, assembly procedures and quality checks,” ISRO added. It also said that the mechanical interfaces have been strengthened with redundancy in the sealing systems and adequacy of the design margins have been verified. “The updates in assembly procedures and non-destructive tests (NDT) during the various phases of integration and transportation have been implemented and the new version of the PS3 solid motor stage is realised and tested successfully,” ISRO said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Based on the detailed analysis and reviews of the test data, the space agency said further tests are planned.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture. India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: critical minerals / minerals / exports / economy, business and finance / business (general)

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: India must improve ties with Bangladesh, and protect Hasina

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The situation puts the Modi government in a spot. Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C. The previous edition of COP30 concluded without a formal roadmap away from fossil fuels — a step back from the COP28 consensus in Dubai. There is a voluntary roadmap ahead of COP31 but it is out of the formal negotiating text. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. 1. Core Context & Background: This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures. One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: award-winning books / books and publishing / Artificial Intelligence

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary. The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board. On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members. The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met. The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights. To be sure, four were nominated immediately to the Gokul board, and they voted with the BJP and its partners to elect a chairman on November 10 . The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government. Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief. The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern . The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident. It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.

1. Core Context & Background: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues. In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Reservation / court / Caste / labour / government / Census 2027

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Kerala Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (KVASU) at Pookode in Wayanad has signed a five-year Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with UAE-based Gulf Medical University (GMU) to promote collaboration in veterinary education and research through its Thumbay College of Veterinary Medicine (TCVM). The agreement envisages student and faculty exchanges, clinical training, internships, veterinary shadowing programmes and summer elective placements. Students from both institutions will have opportunities to undergo clinical training and internships at their respective clinics and hospitals, subject to institutional capacity and academic requirements. The two institutions will also explore collaborative research programmes through the Thumbay Research Institute for Precision Medicine. The MoU provides for faculty exchanges for teaching, research and healthcare management, besides joint continuing veterinary education programmes, workshops and conferences in areas of mutual interest. Another component of the agreement is the possibility of KVASU faculty members who meet GMU’s eligibility criteria being granted adjunct faculty status at TCVM. Such appointments will be formalised through separate agreements. The collaboration will be guided by the One Health approach, which recognises the interconnected health of humans, animals and ecosystems. A coordination committee comprising one representative from each institution will be constituted to oversee the collaboration. The committee would submit reports on joint activities every six months. The MoU was signed by Dr. Manda Venkataramana, Chancellor of GMU, and Dr. Sabin George, Registrar of KVASU.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Officials said the MoU would remain in force for five years and might be renewed following a review of the mutual benefits. It does not entail any immediate financial commitment for either institution. The academic and financial implications of individual programmes will be determined through separate agreements.

The confirmation has triggered a full-scale containment operation, with the Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services Department culling all birds in the affected farm and within a one-kilometre radius of the epicentre. According to Mr. Senthil Kumar: “As many as 35,647 bird deaths were recorded in the affected belt till November 13, since the first case of sudden mortality was reported from a farm at Thamanampatti village in Thiyagavalli Panchayat on October 30.” He added, “Veterinary teams that visited the farm on the day of the first report collected samples and sent them to the Poultry Disease Diagnostic Laboratory (PDDL) in Namakkal.” As deaths mounted in neighbouring farms, further samples were routed to Poultry Disease Diagnosis and Surveillance Laboratory (PDDL) Erode and the Central University Laboratory (CUL) at Madhavaram in Chennai. On November 5, a carcass sample was despatched to NIHSAD Bhopal, which confirmed H5N1 on November 13, he said. Following the standard operating procedure under the National Action Plan, the district was divided into compartments to restrict the spread of the disease. “Initially, we sent only one sample. But a total of 15 farms are affected, of which all the birds in 10 farms have already been wiped out. So only five farms remain, and we are going to cull all [the birds] anyway. As many as nine Rapid Response Teams have been deployed for this purpose,” the Collector said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: So far, 1,550 birds have been humanely culled, and the department is working to cull 100% of the birds in the epicentre farm and within the 1-km radius, in accordance with the Government of India guidelines, 2021.

ಪರಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಜಾತಿಗಳ ಮೀಸಲಾತಿಯನ್ನು ಶೇ.15ರಿಂದ ಶೇ.17ಕ್ಕೆ ಹಾಗೂ ಪರಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಪಂಗಡಗಳ ಮೀಸಲಾತಿಯನ್ನು ಶೇ.3ರಿಂದ ಶೇ.7ಕ್ಕೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸುವ ಉದ್ದೇಶದಿಂದ ಜಾರಿಗೊಳಿಸಲಾದ ಕರ್ನಾಟಕ ಪರಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಜಾತಿ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಪಂಗಡಗಳ (ಶೈಕ್ಷಣಿಕ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಹಾಗೂ ರಾಜ್ಯ ಸರ್ಕಾರಿ ಸೇವೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ನೇಮಕಾತಿ ಅಥವಾ ಹುದ್ದೆಗಳ ಮೀಸಲಾತಿ) ಕಾಯ್ದೆ, 2022 ಅನ್ನು ಸಂವಿಧಾನದ 9ನೇ ಅನುಸೂಚಿಗೆ ಸೇರಿಸುವಂತೆ ಕೋರಿ ಗೌರವಾನ್ವಿತ ಪ್ರಧಾನಮಂತ್ರಿಗಳಾದ ಶ್ರೀ ನರೇಂದ್ರ ಮೋದಿ, ಗೃಹ ಸಚಿವರಾದ ಶ್ರೀ ಅಮಿತ್‌ ಶಾ ಹಾಗೂ ಕೇಂದ್ರ ಸಾಮಾಜಿಕ ನ್ಯಾಯ ಮತ್ತು ಸಬಲೀಕರಣ ಸಚಿವರಾದ ಶ್ರೀ ಡಾ.ವೀರೇಂದ್ರ ಕುಮಾರ್‌ ಅವರಿಗೆ ಪತ್ರ ಬರೆದಿದ್ದೇನೆ. ಸುಮಾರು ಏಳು ದಶಕಗಳಿಂದ ಪರಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಜಾತಿ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಪಂಗಡಗಳ ಮೀಸಲಾತಿ ಪ್ರಮಾಣ ಬದಲಾಗದೆ ಉಳಿದಿತ್ತು. ಈ ಸಮುದಾಯಗಳ ಜನಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯ ಹೆಚ್ಚಳ, ಸಾಮಾಜಿಕ ಮತ್ತು ಶೈಕ್ಷಣಿಕ ಹಿಂದುಳಿದಿರುವಿಕೆ ಹಾಗೂ ನ್ಯಾಯಮೂರ್ತಿ ಎಚ್.ಎನ್. ನಾಗಮೋಹನ್ ದಾಸ್ ಆಯೋಗದ ಶಿಫಾರಸುಗಳನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಮೀಸಲಾತಿ ಪ್ರಮಾಣವನ್ನು ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸಲಾಗಿತ್ತು. ಈ ಕಾಯ್ದೆಗೆ ಸಂವಿಧಾನಾತ್ಮಕ ರಕ್ಷಣೆ ಒದಗಿಸಲು 9ನೇ ಅನುಸೂಚಿಗೆ ಸೇರಿಸಬೇಕೆಂದೂ ಆಯೋಗ ಶಿಫಾರಸು ಮಾಡಿತ್ತು. ಆದರೆ, ಒಟ್ಟು ಮೀಸಲಾತಿ ಶೇ.56ಕ್ಕೆ ಏರಿಕೆಯಾಗಿರುವುದು ಸಂವಿಧಾನಾತ್ಮಕವಾಗಿ ನಿಗದಿಪಡಿಸಲಾದ ಶೇ.50ರ ಮಿತಿಯನ್ನು ಮೀರುತ್ತದೆ ಎಂಬ ಕಾರಣಕ್ಕೆ ಕರ್ನಾಟಕ ಹೈಕೋರ್ಟ್ 2026ರ ಅಕ್ಟೋಬರ್ 12ರಂದು ಮೀಸಲಾತಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚಳದ ನಿಬಂಧನೆಗಳನ್ನು ರದ್ದುಗೊಳಿಸಿದೆ. ಈ ತೀರ್ಪಿನ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ರಾಜ್ಯ ಸರ್ಕಾರ ಸುಪ್ರೀಂ ಕೋರ್ಟ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಮೇಲ್ಮನವಿ ಸಲ್ಲಿಸಿದೆ. 1994ರಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂವಿಧಾನದ 76ನೇ ತಿದ್ದುಪಡಿಯ ಮೂಲಕ ತಮಿಳುನಾಡಿನ ಶೇ.69ರ ಮೀಸಲಾತಿ ಕಾಯ್ದೆಯನ್ನು 9ನೇ ಅನುಸೂಚಿಗೆ ಸೇರಿಸಲಾಗಿತ್ತು. ಅದೇ ಮಾದರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಕರ್ನಾಟಕದ ಶೇ.56ರ ಒಟ್ಟು ಮೀಸಲಾತಿಯ ಭಾಗವಾಗಿರುವ ಪರಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಜಾತಿಗಳ ಶೇ.17 ಹಾಗೂ ಪರಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಪಂಗಡಗಳ ಶೇ.7ರ ಮೀಸಲಾತಿಗೂ ಸಂವಿಧಾನಾತ್ಮಕ ರಕ್ಷಣೆ ಒದಗಿಸುವ ಕುರಿತು ಕೇಂದ್ರ ಸರ್ಕಾರ ಗಂಭೀರವಾಗಿ ಪರಿಗಣಿಸಬೇಕು. ಕರ್ನಾಟಕ ಸರ್ಕಾರವು 2023ರ ಮಾರ್ಚ್ 23ರಂದೇ ಈ ಸಂಬಂಧ ಕೇಂದ್ರ ಸರ್ಕಾರಕ್ಕೆ ಪ್ರಸ್ತಾವನೆ ಸಲ್ಲಿಸಿತ್ತು. 2025ರ ಡಿಸೆಂಬರ್ 18ರಂದು ರಾಜ್ಯ ವಿಧಾನಸಭೆಯಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ನಿರ್ಣಯ ಅಂಗೀಕರಿಸಲಾಗಿತ್ತು. ನಿಕಟಪೂರ್ವ ಮುಖ್ಯಮಂತ್ರಿಗಳಾದ ಶ್ರೀ ಸಿದ್ದರಾಮಯ್ಯ ಅವರು 2026ರ ಏಪ್ರಿಲ್ 16ರಂದು ಪ್ರಧಾನಮಂತ್ರಿಗಳಿಗೆ ಪತ್ರ ಬರೆದು ಇದೇ ಬೇಡಿಕೆಯನ್ನು ಪುನರುಚ್ಚರಿಸಿದ್ದರು. ಈ ಹಿನ್ನೆಲೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಧಾನಮಂತ್ರಿಗಳ ವೈಯಕ್ತಿಕ ಮಧ್ಯಪ್ರವೇಶವನ್ನು ಕೋರಿ ಪತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಮುಖವಾಗಿ ಈ ಕೆಳಗಿನ ಬೇಡಿಕೆಗಳನ್ನು ಮುಂದಿಟ್ಟಿದ್ದೇನೆ. 1. ಪರಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಜಾತಿಗಳ ಮೀಸಲಾತಿಯನ್ನು ಶೇ.17ಕ್ಕೆ ಹಾಗೂ ಪರಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಪಂಗಡಗಳ ಮೀಸಲಾತಿಯನ್ನು ಶೇ.7ಕ್ಕೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸುವ ಕರ್ನಾಟಕದ ಕಾಯ್ದೆಯನ್ನು ಸಂವಿಧಾನದ 9ನೇ ಅನುಸೂಚಿಗೆ ಸೇರಿಸಬೇಕು. 2. ಕಾಯ್ದೆಗೆ ಸಂವಿಧಾನಾತ್ಮಕ ರಕ್ಷಣೆ ಒದಗಿಸಲು ಅಗತ್ಯವಾದ ಸಂವಿಧಾನ ತಿದ್ದುಪಡಿ ಮಸೂದೆಯನ್ನು ಸಂಸತ್ತಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಮಂಡಿಸುವ ಪ್ರಕ್ರಿಯೆಯನ್ನು ಕೇಂದ್ರ ಸರ್ಕಾರ ತುರ್ತಾಗಿ ಆರಂಭಿಸಬೇಕು. 3. ರಾಷ್ಟ್ರೀಯ ಪರಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಜಾತಿ ಆಯೋಗ ಹಾಗೂ ರಾಷ್ಟ್ರೀಯ ಪರಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಪಂಗಡಗಳ ಆಯೋಗಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಸಮಾಲೋಚನೆ ನಡೆಸಿ, ನ್ಯಾಯಾಲಯ ಗುರುತಿಸಿರುವ ಸಂವಿಧಾನಾತ್ಮಕ ಹಾಗೂ ಪ್ರಕ್ರಿಯಾತ್ಮಕ ಸಮಸ್ಯೆಗಳನ್ನು ಪರಿಹರಿಸಲು ಕ್ರಮ ಕೈಗೊಳ್ಳಬೇಕು. 4. ಕೇಂದ್ರ ಕಾನೂನು ಮತ್ತು ನ್ಯಾಯ ಸಚಿವಾಲಯ, ಸಾಮಾಜಿಕ ನ್ಯಾಯ ಮತ್ತು ಸಬಲೀಕರಣ ಸಚಿವಾಲಯ, ಬುಡಕಟ್ಟು ವ್ಯವಹಾರಗಳ ಸಚಿವಾಲಯ ಹಾಗೂ ಗೃಹ ಸಚಿವಾಲಯಗಳು ಸಮನ್ವಯದಿಂದ ಕಾರ್ಯನಿರ್ವಹಿಸಿ, ಕಾಲಮಿತಿಯೊಳಗೆ ಸೂಕ್ತ ಸಂವಿಧಾನಾತ್ಮಕ ಮತ್ತು ಶಾಸನಾತ್ಮಕ ಕ್ರಮಗಳನ್ನು ಕೈಗೊಳ್ಳಬೇಕು. 5. ದೇಶದ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತಿರುವ ಸಾಮಾಜಿಕ ವಾಸ್ತವಗಳು, ವಿವಿಧ ರಾಜ್ಯಗಳ ಅನುಭವಗಳು ಹಾಗೂ ಸಮಾನತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಸಾಮಾಜಿಕ ನ್ಯಾಯದ ಸಂವಿಧಾನಾತ್ಮಕ ತತ್ವಗಳನ್ನು ಪರಿಗಣಿಸಿ, ಶೇ.50ರ ಮೀಸಲಾತಿ ಮಿತಿಯ ಪ್ರಸ್ತುತತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಅನ್ವಯದ ಕುರಿತು ರಾಷ್ಟ್ರಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ವ್ಯಾಪಕ ಸಮಾಲೋಚನೆ ನಡೆಸಬೇಕು. ತಮಿಳುನಾಡಿನ ಶೇ.69ರ ಮೀಸಲಾತಿಗೆ ಸಂವಿಧಾನಾತ್ಮಕ ರಕ್ಷಣೆ ಒದಗಿಸಿರುವಂತೆ, ಕರ್ನಾಟಕದ ಶೇ.56ರ ಒಟ್ಟು ಮೀಸಲಾತಿಯ ಭಾಗವಾಗಿರುವ ಪರಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಜಾತಿ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಪಂಗಡಗಳ ಶೇ.24ರ ಒಟ್ಟು ಮೀಸಲಾತಿಗೂ ಸಂವಿಧಾನಾತ್ಮಕ ರಕ್ಷಣೆ ದೊರೆಯಬೇಕೆಂಬುದು ನಮ್ಮ ಆಗ್ರಹವಾಗಿದೆ. ಸಾಮಾಜಿಕ ನ್ಯಾಯದ ವಿಚಾರವು ರಾಜಕೀಯ ಪಕ್ಷಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಸರ್ಕಾರಗಳ ನಡುವಿನ ಭಿನ್ನಾಭಿಪ್ರಾಯಗಳನ್ನು ಮೀರಿದ್ದಾಗಿದೆ. ಸಂವಿಧಾನ ಶಿಲ್ಪಿ ಡಾ. ಬಿ.ಆರ್. ಅಂಬೇಡ್ಕರ್ ಅವರ ಆಶಯದಂತೆ ಐತಿಹಾಸಿಕವಾಗಿ ಅವಕಾಶವಂಚಿತರಾದ ಸಮುದಾಯಗಳಿಗೆ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣ ಮತ್ತು ಉದ್ಯೋಗದಲ್ಲಿ ನ್ಯಾಯಯುತ ಅವಕಾಶಗಳನ್ನು ಕಲ್ಪಿಸುವುದು ನಮ್ಮೆಲ್ಲರ ಸಾಮೂಹಿಕ ಜವಾಬ್ದಾರಿಯಾಗಿದೆ. ಪರಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಜಾತಿ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಪಂಗಡಗಳ ಲಕ್ಷಾಂತರ ಜನರ ಭವಿಷ್ಯಕ್ಕೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸಿದ ಈ ಮಹತ್ವದ ವಿಷಯವನ್ನು ರಾಷ್ಟ್ರೀಯ ಸಂವಿಧಾನಾತ್ಮಕ ಮಹತ್ವದ ವಿಚಾರವಾಗಿ ಪರಿಗಣಿಸಿ, ಕರ್ನಾಟಕದ ದೀರ್ಘಕಾಲದ ಪ್ರಸ್ತಾವನೆ ಕುರಿತು ಕೇಂದ್ರ ಸರ್ಕಾರ ಸಕಾರಾತ್ಮಕ ಹಾಗೂ ಕಾಲಮಿತಿಯೊಳಗಿನ ನಿರ್ಧಾರ ಕೈಗೊಂಡು ಅಗತ್ಯ ಶಾಸನಾತ್ಮಕ ಕ್ರಮಗಳನ್ನು ಜರುಗಿಸಬೇಕು ಎಂದು ಮನವಿ ಮಾಡಿದ್ದೇನೆ. The enhanced reservation was recommended by a commission headed by retired Karnataka High Court judge H.N. Nagamohan Das. The State subsequently enacted the Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Reservation of Seats in Educational Institutions and of Appointments or Posts in the Services under the State) Act, 2022. The legislation received the Governor’s assent on January 11, 2023, and came into effect retrospectively from November 1, 2022, the letter stated. The State had submitted its proposal to the Union Government on March 23, 2023 , seeking inclusion of the legislation in the Ninth Schedule. The Legislative Assembly also passed a resolution on December 18, 2025, urging the Centre to provide constitutional protection to the enhanced reservation. The Union Government had acknowledged the receipt of Karnataka’s proposal in a written reply in the Lok Sabha on July 25, 2026, but said inclusion in the Ninth Schedule was not considered appropriate at that stage as the matter was pending before the High Court.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Parameshwara has also called for consultations with the National Commissions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes to address the constitutional and procedural issues concerning the legislation. He has sought coordinated action by the Ministries of Law and Justice, Social Justice and Empowerment, Tribal Affairs, and Home Affairs to expedite the matter.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The State Government has decided to purchase 24 new cars for the official use of the Ministers and the Chief Secretary on the grounds that the existing vehicles have “considerably deteriorated in their mechanical condition due to prolonged use.” The General Administration Department has issued orders for the purchase of 24 Toyota Innova Hycross (ZX(O) Strong Hybrid) vehicles which include 22 for the use of the Ministers and Chief Secretary Bishwananth Sinha and two for the use of State guests. The procurement is estimated to cost ₹9.60 crore, but the actual expenditure would be determined based on the prevailing rates and applicable charges at the time of procurement, the GAD order noted. The decision has sparked a debate as Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan, on taking charge in May this year, had decided to use a car that was already in use, saying that the Government would forego unnecessary expenditure amid financial stress. He had also decided to do away with the Chief Minister’s motorcade. In September, the Minister for Local Bodies K. M. Shaji’s decision to use a luxury sports utility vehicle, purportedly borrowed from a businessperson friend of his, as his official vehicle had courted controversy. According to the November 12 order, the Tourism Department has been entrusted with the task of procuring the vehicles. The vehicles presently being used by most of the Ministers for official purposes have become old and have considerably deteriorated in their mechanical condition due to prolonged use, the GAD order noted. “They require frequent repairs and maintenance, resulting in increased expenditure and affecting their reliability and availability for official duties. The need for suitable and well-maintained vehicles for the Ministers to attend official engagements, meetings, field visits and various government functions also necessitates the periodic replacement of the existing vehicles,” it said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Vehicles presently available with the government for protocol purposes are also inadequate to meet the growing requirements arising from the visits of VIPs, foreign dignitaries and other distinguished guests to the State, the Department noted.

itemListElement.headline: Karnataka Deputy CM Parameshwara writes to Modi, Shah seeking inclusion of State’s SC/ST reservation law in Ninth Schedule on the lines of Tamil Nadu
itemListElement.description: 1. Core Context & Background: Citing Tamil Nadu’s 69% reservation framework as a precedent, Mr. Parameshwara said Karnataka deserved equal consideration and a constitutional amendment to safeguard the rights and opportunities of SC/ST communities.

itemListElement.headline: Keralam Government to buy new vehicles for Ministers and Chief Secretary
itemListElement.description: 1. Core Context & Background: The General Administration Department has issued orders for the purchase of 24 Toyota Innova Hycross ZX(O) Strong Hybrid vehicles which include 22 for the use of the Ministers and Chief Secretary Bishwananth Sinha and two for the use of State guests
